rules.quote: but such contribution to the sinking fund shall not be less than ten per cent of the charges.
rules.applies: Governs the sinking fund rate. Ten per cent of the charges is the floor. At RM 200 in charges, the floor is RM 20, not RM 12. Applies even though the additional by-law sets 6%, because the Act governs.

rules.applies: Sets 6%, which is below the Act's floor. Conflicts with section 61(3) of the Act. Under the precedence rule the Act governs, so this sub-rule cannot be applied to set the sinking fund below 10%. The charges figure of RM 200 in ABL-8(1) is consistent with the bill.

rules.quote: Interest on late payment is charged at 10% a year on a daily basis, as provided in by-law 6(2) of the Third Schedule.
rules.applies: Sets the late interest rate at 10% a year, daily. Within the cap in section 60(3)(c) of the Act. Whether interest is due for the 20-day delay depends on the notice date (see BL-6).

rules.applies: Stains on the bathroom ceiling of B-08-04 are 'inter-floor leakage' as defined: evidence of dampness, moisture or water penetration on a ceiling forming part of the interior of a parcel. This makes the Regulation 56 to 58 process relevant. It is a report until inspected.

Inspection duty: the management corporation (through the office) must inspect the affected parcel, any other parcel and the common property as soon as practically possible, or within seven days from receipt of a notice under regulation 56, to find the cause and the party responsible. Officer to confirm whether this walk-in report is to be treated as a regulation 56 notice; if so, the seven-day limit runs from receipt.

Decides responsibility only after inspection. Under the presumption in section 142 of the Act (as referred to in REG-58(a)), the defect is presumed to be in the parcel above, unless the evidence shows otherwise. A defect in a water or drainage pipe serving more than one parcel is common property (REG-58(b)); one serving only one parcel is that parcel's defect (REG-58(c)). Until the source is verified, no party is responsible and no one is named as the cause.

Access to the unit above (or any other parcel) for inspection needs seven days' written notice, except in an emergency (REG-63(3)). Give written notice to the unit above as soon as the inspection date is set. If the water becomes a flood or danger, emergency access applies.

After inspection, decide the cause and responsible party under REG-58: parcel defect (unit above) or common property defect. Do not name a party until verified.

If the inspection shows the fault is in common property (for example a shared pipe under REG-58(b)), log a maintenance work order and give the resident the reference number. If it is in a single parcel, tell the resident which parcel's owner must repair it.

facts_known: Parcel B-04-02, Block B, floor 4, occupied by a tenant, 10 share units.
November bill shows maintenance charges of RM 200 and sinking fund of RM 12.

Whether the complainant is the account holder or the owner, and whether the bill is addressed to the parcel.

rules.quote: such contribution to the sinking fund shall not be less than ten per cent of the charges
rules.applies: Sets the sinking fund floor at 10% of charges unless a general meeting determines otherwise. On RM 200 charges this is RM 20, not RM 12. The Act governs over the additional by-law on this point.

rules.quote: The contribution to the sinking fund is 6% of the charges.
rules.applies: Sets the sinking fund at 6%, which on RM 200 gives RM 12 as billed. This is below the Act's 10% floor, so it does not hold on this point.

rules.quote: The charges payable for the maintenance account are RM 200 a month for each parcel
rules.applies: Confirms the RM 200 monthly charges as billed. No conflict.

rules.quote: at the expiry of the period of fourteen days of receiving a notice from the management corporation
rules.applies: A parcel becomes a defaulter, and interest can run, only after 14 days from receiving a notice. The 20-day lateness alone does not show interest was properly charged; the notice date is needed.

rules.quote: the proprietor shall pay interest at the rate of ten per cent per annum on a daily basis
rules.applies: Interest rate on unpaid sums after the 14-day period. The amount billed must be checked against this rate and start date.

rules.quote: which shall not exceed the rate of ten per cent per annum
rules.applies: Caps late payment interest at 10% a year. The late interest billed must fall within this cap.

conflict.governs: ACT-s61 (Strata Management Act 2013, section 61(3)) governs over ABL-8(2) (Additional By-law 8(2)).
conflict.why: The Act sets the sinking fund at not less than 10% of charges unless a general meeting decides otherwise, while the additional by-law sets 6%. Under the precedence in SOP-3 the Act governs, so the 6% rate cannot be relied on to bill below 10% unless a general meeting has determined a rate. This is a difference between documents, so it is not a handover reason; the office should check the position and state the governing rule.
